barrier.off_rating_high.note: …and the 99.9th percentile, the high side; averaged over the panel's 3 seeds

barrier.off_rating_high_seed_ratio.note: how many times the barrier-off arm's 99.9th rating percentile moved between the panel's seeds — the blow-out HAPPENS every time, while its size is not itself a reproducible quantity, which is what an unbounded tail does

barrier.off_rating_low.note: 0.1th percentile of the derived rating with the slope barrier removed — the low side of the blow-out. A per-fit property, averaged over the panel's 3 seeds

barrier.off_slope_at_floor_pct.note: share of slopes on the clamp with the barrier removed, averaged over the panel's 3 seeds

barrier.off_stop_cost_mnat.note: the same paired held-out cost read at the FINAL epoch — the fit that would actually ship, averaged over the panel's 3 seeds

barrier.off_stop_cost_sign_consistent.note: 1 when every seed puts the barrier-off cost on the same side of zero on BOTH readings, 0 when the seeds disagree. An indicator for a `fig-guard: barrier.off_stop_cost_sign_consistent == 1` beside any sentence naming the direction of that cost, never for a span

barrier.off_stop_tail_cost_mnat.note: held-out (stop-split) cost of removing the barrier over the last third of the budget, millinats — PAIRED against the shipped arm of its own seed, then meaned over the seeds. The headline reading: it is the level the arm settled at, which a final checkpoint alone samples only once

barrier.shipped_no_rating_max.note: and the most, in a run differing only in the seed. The pair is the figure: this count is a property of a particular fit and not of the model, so it is re-read after a refit rather than carried

barrier.shipped_no_rating_min.note: fewest problems left with no defined rating — a floor at or above the calibration probability — across the panel's runs of the SHIPPED configuration

barrier.shipped_rating_span.note: p0.1..p99.9 span of the derived rating as SHIPPED, the same per-fit property the two arms above are compared against, averaged over the panel's 3 seeds — without it neither blow-out nor compression has a reference

barrier.shipped_wander_range_mnat.note: the same wander as a peak-to-peak range, averaged over the seeds — how far apart two honest single-arm readings of one configuration can land

barrier.shipped_wander_sd_mnat.note: standard deviation of the SHIPPED arm's own held-out score across the last third of its budget, millinats, averaged over the seeds — the panel's resolution floor. No contrast smaller than this is resolved by one arm per configuration, which is why every configuration here is replicated

barrier.tenx_cost_sign_consistent.note: 1 when every seed puts the ten-times cost on the same side of zero on both readings. An indicator for a fig-guard, not a span

barrier.tenx_no_rating_mean.note: the same count at ten times the barrier weight, seed-averaged — the one cost of a heavier barrier the held-out likelihood cannot show, since the problems it touches ship a sentinel rather than a wrong number

barrier.tenx_no_rating_sign_consistent.note: 1 when the heavier barrier moves the undefined-rating count the same way at every seed, 0 when it does not. A 0 says this count does not establish a cost for the heavier weight — the count is unstable under BOTH weights, so a difference between two single runs of them is not a difference between the weights

barrier.tenx_rating_span.note: p0.1..p99.9 span of the derived rating at ten times the barrier weight — the compression the weight is swept against. A per-fit property, averaged over the panel's 3 seeds

barrier.tenx_stop_cost_mnat.note: the same cost read at the FINAL epoch, averaged over the panel's 3 seeds

barrier.tenx_stop_tail_cost_mnat.note: held-out cost of TEN TIMES the barrier weight over the last third of the budget, millinats, paired within a seed and then meaned, averaged over the panel's 3 seeds. §1.7 chooses the weight by held-out sweep and names ten times as the failure direction, so where that arm lands is part of the claim: negative means the heavier barrier fits BETTER than what ships

blocks.problem_all_delta_final_mnat.note: the same three-seed average on held-out PROBLEMS, whose parameters come from the feature trunk alone (the reading §1.3's feature-side claim is about), read at the final epoch alone, where one checkpoint is one draw from the settled trace's own wander

blocks.problem_all_delta_mnat.note: held-out delta of the answer-derived blocks added back against the shipped trunk input, millinats, scored on held-out PROBLEMS, whose parameters come from the feature trunk alone (the reading §1.3's feature-side claim is about), averaged over three seeds; each seed's delta is PAIRED (same rows held aside) and read as the mean over the last third of the budget. Positive means the added blocks fit worse. Not comparable with the other unit's delta

blocks.problem_all_delta_seed0_mnat.note: the within-seed paired delta at seed 0 on held-out PROBLEMS, whose parameters come from the feature trunk alone (the reading §1.3's feature-side claim is about), millinats, last third of the budget — one of the three that unit's headline averages; deltas from different seeds are different holdout draws, and deltas from different units are different quantities

blocks.problem_all_delta_seed1_mnat.note: the within-seed paired delta at seed 1 on held-out PROBLEMS, whose parameters come from the feature trunk alone (the reading §1.3's feature-side claim is about), millinats, last third of the budget — one of the three that unit's headline averages; deltas from different seeds are different holdout draws, and deltas from different units are different quantities

blocks.problem_all_delta_seed2_mnat.note: the within-seed paired delta at seed 2 on held-out PROBLEMS, whose parameters come from the feature trunk alone (the reading §1.3's feature-side claim is about), millinats, last third of the budget — one of the three that unit's headline averages; deltas from different seeds are different holdout draws, and deltas from different units are different quantities

blocks.problem_rating_parity_holds.note: THE CLAIM'S TEST: 1 when the answer-conditioning contrast on held-out PROBLEMS, whose parameters come from the feature trunk alone (the reading §1.3's feature-side claim is about) sits inside that same reading's replicate spread, 0 when it does not. The rule, in full and with no threshold in it: the absolute value of blocks.problem_all_delta_mnat is no greater than blocks.problem_shipped_seed_spread_mnat — the averaged paired delta against the between-seed range of the shipped arm's last-third mean score, both in millinats and both from the same unit. An indicator for a fig-guard, not a span

blocks.problem_shipped_seed_spread_mnat.note: replicate spread of the SHIPPED configuration on held-out PROBLEMS, whose parameters come from the feature trunk alone (the reading §1.3's feature-side claim is about): the range (max minus min) over the three seeds of its own last-third mean held-out score, millinats — one configuration, three seeds, so it is scatter alone

blocks.row_all_delta_mnat.note: held-out delta of the answer-derived blocks added back against the shipped trunk input, millinats, scored on held-out ROWS of problems the fit has otherwise seen (the shipped fit's own convergence split), averaged over three seeds; each seed's delta is PAIRED (same rows held aside) and read as the mean over the last third of the budget. blocks.row_all_delta_seed0_mnat.note: the within-seed paired delta at seed 0 on held-out ROWS of problems the fit has otherwise seen (the shipped fit's own convergence split), millinats, last third of the budget — one of the three that unit's headline averages; deltas from different seeds are different holdout draws, and deltas from different units are different quantities

blocks.row_all_delta_seed1_mnat.note: the within-seed paired delta at seed 1 on held-out ROWS of problems the fit has otherwise seen (the shipped fit's own convergence split), millinats, last third of the budget — one of the three that unit's headline averages; deltas from different seeds are different holdout draws, and deltas from different units are different quantities

blocks.row_all_delta_seed2_mnat.note: the within-seed paired delta at seed 2 on held-out ROWS of problems the fit has otherwise seen (the shipped fit's own convergence split), millinats, last third of the budget — one of the three that unit's headline averages; deltas from different seeds are different holdout draws, and deltas from different units are different quantities

regularization.decay_both_off_cost_mnat.note: the held-out-PROBLEM cost of weight decay in place of both dropouts, against the shipped fit, in millinats over the last third of the budget and signed (positive = worse than shipped). PAIRED inside a seed — both arms hold aside the same problems — and then averaged over the panel's 2 seeds

regularization.decay_both_off_cost_sign_.note: 1 when both seeds put the cost of weight decay in place of both dropouts on the same side of zero on the last-third reading, 0 when they disagree — the two seeds being independent estimates of one paired delta. An indicator for a fig-guard beside a sentence naming that contrast's direction, not for a span

regularization.decay_cost_final_mnat.note: the same paired cost of adding weight decay with both dropouts intact, read at the final epoch alone, where one checkpoint is one draw from the settled trace's own wander, averaged over the panel's 2 seeds

regularization.decay_cost_mnat.note: the held-out-PROBLEM cost of adding weight decay with both dropouts intact, against the shipped fit, in millinats over the last third of the budget and signed (positive = worse than shipped). PAIRED inside a seed — both arms hold aside the same problems — and then averaged over the panel's 2 seeds

regularization.decay_cost_sign_consisten.note: 1 when both seeds put the cost of adding weight decay with both dropouts intact on the same side of zero on the last-third reading, 0 when they disagree — the two seeds being independent estimates of one paired delta. An indicator for a fig-guard beside a sentence naming that contrast's direction, not for a span

regularization.decay_gain_is_field_ridge.note: THE ATTRIBUTION of the decay arm's held-out gain: 1 when, at every seed, decaying network AND fields beats the shipped fit while decaying the network alone is worse than it — i.e. the gain belongs entirely to the L2 the fields receive, an ability ridge that re-gauges the fit rather than regularizing the network. A fig-guard's figure for the sentence declining to adopt the decay

regularization.decay_net_cost_final_mnat.note: the same paired cost of adding the same weight decay to the network alone, the per-user fields exempt, read at the final epoch alone, where one checkpoint is one draw from the settled trace's own wander, averaged over the panel's 2 seeds

regularization.decay_net_cost_mnat.note: the held-out-PROBLEM cost of adding the same weight decay to the network alone, the per-user fields exempt, against the shipped fit, in millinats over the last third of the budget and signed (positive = worse than shipped). PAIRED inside a seed — both arms hold aside the same problems — and then averaged over the panel's 2 seeds

regularization.decay_net_cost_sign_consi.note: 1 when both seeds put the cost of adding the same weight decay to the network alone, the per-user fields exempt on the same side of zero on the last-third reading, 0 when they disagree — the two seeds being independent estimates of one paired delta. An indicator for a fig-guard beside a sentence naming that contrast's direction, not for a span

regularization.decay_no_substitute.note: §1.5'S CLAIM as an indicator: 1 when weight decay does not substitute for dropout — the arm carrying decay with both dropouts off is NO BETTER held out than the arm carrying nothing at all, its cost against the shipped fit being at least the 'both_off' arm's, at every seed. 0 means decay recovered part of what dropout was doing at some seed. The claim is one-sided: it says decay buys back none of that cost, not that decay is itself harmful

regularization.decay_substitution_gap_mn.note: the within-seed paired difference between the 'decay_both_off' arm and the 'both_off' arm, millinats on the last-third reading, averaged over the panel's 2 seeds. Positive means weight decay left a dropout-free fit WORSE than no regularization at all; around zero that it changed nothing; negative that it recovered some of what dropout was doing

regularization.input_off_cost_final_mnat.note: the same paired cost of removing the feature region's column dropout, read at the final epoch alone, where one checkpoint is one draw from the settled trace's own wander, averaged over the panel's 2 seeds

regularization.input_off_cost_mnat.note: the held-out-PROBLEM cost of removing the feature region's column dropout, against the shipped fit, in millinats over the last third of the budget and signed (positive = worse than shipped). PAIRED inside a seed — both arms hold aside the same problems — and then averaged over the panel's 2 seeds

regularization.input_off_cost_sign_consi.note: 1 when both seeds put the cost of removing the feature region's column dropout on the same side of zero on the last-third reading, 0 when they disagree — the two seeds being independent estimates of one paired delta. An indicator for a fig-guard beside a sentence naming that contrast's direction, not for a span

regularization.shipped_wander_range_mnat.note: the resolution floor every contrast here is read against: the shipped arm's own peak-to-peak held-out spread across the last third of ITS OWN run, millinats, averaged over the panel's 2 seeds. One configuration at one seed, so it is wander and nothing else

regularization.superadditive_every_seed.note: 1 when that excess over additivity is positive at EVERY seed, 0 otherwise — never an average, which one seed could carry alone. The indicator §1.5's 'strongly super-additive' rests on; a fig-guard's figure, not a span's

regularization.superadditive_excess_fina.note: the same excess over additivity read at the final epoch alone — `regularization.superadditive_excess_mnat` on one checkpoint instead of the last third, and therefore carrying the settled trace's full wander

regularization.superadditive_excess_mnat.note: THE EXCESS OVER ADDITIVITY, in millinats, and not a total: the held-out cost of removing dropout at BOTH sites MINUS the sum of the costs of removing it at each site alone, every term a within-seed paired cost against the shipped fit on the last-third reading, the excess formed inside a seed and then averaged over the panel's 2 seeds. Positive means the two removals compound (§1.5's super-additivity), zero that they merely add, negative that they overlap

regularization.trunk_off_cost_final_mnat.note: the same paired cost of removing the trunk's dropout, read at the final epoch alone, where one checkpoint is one draw from the settled trace's own wander, averaged over the panel's 2 seeds

regularization.trunk_off_cost_mnat.note: the held-out-PROBLEM cost of removing the trunk's dropout, against the shipped fit, in millinats over the last third of the budget and signed (positive = worse than shipped). PAIRED inside a seed — both arms hold aside the same problems — and then averaged over the panel's 2 seeds

regularization.trunk_off_cost_sign_consi.note: 1 when both seeds put the cost of removing the trunk's dropout on the same side of zero on the last-third reading, 0 when they disagree — the two seeds being independent estimates of one paired delta. An indicator for a fig-guard beside a sentence naming that contrast's direction, not for a span

schedule.budgets_swept.note: distinct cosine epoch budgets the panel runs on the held-out problem unit, each with its own replicated arms — a shorter cosine run is not a prefix of a longer one, so every point is its own fit

schedule.constant_epoch_draw_mnat.note: mean over those runs of (the single held-out score at 80% of the budget - the run's final level), millinats: how much what ships depends on where the budget happens to fall

schedule.constant_initializations.note: runs of the retired constant schedule at 3000 epochs behind the reference level, all on held-out problems at one pinned draw, differing only in the seed

schedule.constant_level_sd_mnat.note: run-to-run sd of that constant configuration's final level (mean of the last 2% of checkpoints) on held-out problems, millinats

schedule.constant_long_level_cost_mnat.note: final level of the constant schedule run to 7000 epochs minus its own 3000-epoch level, held-out problems, millinats — positive means the undecayed fit also gets worse when given the longer budget

schedule.overfit_budget.note: smallest cosine budget whose final level is worse than the shipping budget's by more than the window's run-to-run sd — the definition of the window's upper bound, not a separate test

schedule.overfit_level_cost_mnat.note: that budget's final level minus the shipping budget's, held-out problems, millinats

schedule.overfit_max_climb_mnat.note: over that budget's runs, the largest (final level - the run's own held-out minimum), millinats: how far past its best point a run finishes, which the decay to zero makes permanent

schedule.overfit_work_epochs.note: that budget's learning-rate integral in constant-rate epochs — the optimization it actually delivered, not its epoch count

schedule.sd_ratio.note: constant-schedule run-to-run sd over the window's, both on held-out problems: how much of the fit's wander the decay takes out of the RESULT rather than out of one run's tail

schedule.sd_ratio_p.note: one-sided F-test p that the constant spread exceeds the window's, at 5 and 6 degrees of freedom — the honest reading of a variance ratio from this few runs

schedule.shipped_budget.note: the cosine epoch budget production trains, read from pipeline.train_mirt and required to be an arm of this panel

schedule.shipped_level_cost_mnat.note: final level of the shipping cosine budget minus the constant baseline's, held-out problems, millinats — negative means the shipped fit generalizes better

schedule.shipped_work_epochs.note: the shipping budget's learning-rate integral in constant-rate epochs

schedule.wall_clock_ratio.note: median wall clock of the shipping cosine arms over the constant baseline's — arms shared a GPU pool, so this tracks the budget ratio rather than timing a run

schedule.window_hi_budget.note: highest cosine budget still level with the shipping one: the walk upward stops before the first budget that is worse by more than the window's own spread

schedule.window_level_cost_mnat.note: the same comparison pooled over every cosine budget in the plateau window, millinats

schedule.window_level_sd_mnat.note: run-to-run sd inside that window, pooled about each budget's own mean, millinats — the spread a paired contrast under the shipped schedule is read against

schedule.window_lo_budget.note: lowest cosine budget in the plateau window, which is the shipping budget by construction

schedule.within_run_range_constant_mnat.note: the band a run wanders inside at its end under the retired CONSTANT rate: peak-to-peak of its held-out-ROW score over the last third of the budget, millinats, averaged over runs

schedule.within_run_range_cosine_mnat.note: the same band under the cosine decay to zero, at the 3000-epoch row-unit arms, the only cosine budget the row unit carries — far narrower almost by construction, since a rate going to zero stops moving the parameters, which is why it settles nothing on its own

seeds.axes_matched.note: axes matched per pair — K as shipped

seeds.problems_scored.note: problems every agreement above is measured over: attempted at least once (first-time attempts) and carried by every arm

seeds.taught_cross_seed_mean.note: the same statistic for two fits of the SHIPPED configuration differing only in the seed — the teaching pull on

seeds.teaching_cost_final_mnat.note: the same cost read at the final epoch alone — the epoch that would actually ship

seeds.teaching_cost_mnat.note: what the constant pull costs on held-out problems, millinats, positive meaning the taught fit predicts worse. Paired: the taught and untaught arms at one seed hold aside the same problems. Each arm is read as the mean over the last third of its budget, the two same-seed pairs then averaged

seeds.teaching_cost_sign_consistent.note: 1 when both same-seed pairs put the cost on the same side of zero under both readings, 0 otherwise. An indicator for a fig-guard: it is what says the sign is a finding rather than the wander of a single pair

seeds.teaching_gap.note: taught minus untaught cross-seed agreement, on the means — what the constant pull toward the rule columns buys in basis stability, the two measured on the same problems

seeds.untaught_cross_seed_mean.note: cross-seed direction agreement with the teaching pull off: axes matched one-to-one between two fits by maximum total |correlation| of their per-problem loadings, each matched pair's |correlation| meaned over the 7 axes and then over the three untaught seed pairs, on attempted problems

seeds.untaught_cross_seed_min.note: the same agreement at each untaught pair's weakest-matched axis, averaged over the three pairs

sefloor.dan_min.note: tightest SE floor over the dan range, in ranks — knots in [+0, +9) in internal rank, the 1d…9d bands

sefloor.kyu_vs_dan_ratio.note: mean floor over the middle kyus ÷ mean floor over the dan range, each an unweighted mean over that region's knots ([-15, -5) in internal rank, the 15k…6k bands; [+0, +9) in internal rank, the 1d…9d bands) — the TYPICAL kyu-vs-dan comparison, not the extremes

sefloor.midkyu_max.note: loosest SE floor over the middle kyus, in ranks — knots in [-15, -5) in internal rank, the 15k…6k bands

sefloor.spread_ratio.note: loosest middle-kyu floor ÷ tightest dan-range floor — the spread between the extremes a constant floor would have to cover

serve.clear_100_300.note: clear rate over positions 101-300; first-time attempts, one row per (user, problem), by 1-based position in the user's own first-time history

serve.clear_25_100.note: clear rate over positions 26-100; first-time attempts, one row per (user, problem), by 1-based position in the user's own first-time history

serve.clear_after300.note: clear rate past position 300; first-time attempts, one row per (user, problem), by 1-based position in the user's own first-time history. Also the rate quoted for users past their first few hundred problems — the same population

serve.clear_first25.note: clear rate over positions 1-25; first-time attempts, one row per (user, problem), by 1-based position in the user's own first-time history

serve.fitted_ceiling.note: 1 − the SHIPPED global lapse: the upper asymptote of the fitted response curve, which no bin of finite gap reaches

serve.gap_100_300.note: mean rating gap over positions 101-300; mean of (the player's own anchor rating − the problem's shipped rating) in rating units, positive when the problem sits BELOW the player; the anchor is their 80%-clear rating fitted over their WHOLE first-time history, so a player needs at least 20 rated attempts and a mixed record to enter; first-time attempts, one row per (user, problem), by 1-based position in the user's own first-time history

serve.gap_25_100.note: mean rating gap over positions 26-100; mean of (the player's own anchor rating − the problem's shipped rating) in rating units, positive when the problem sits BELOW the player; the anchor is their 80%-clear rating fitted over their WHOLE first-time history, so a player needs at least 20 rated attempts and a mixed record to enter; first-time attempts, one row per (user, problem), by 1-based position in the user's own first-time history

serve.gap_after300.note: mean rating gap past position 300; mean of (the player's own anchor rating − the problem's shipped rating) in rating units, positive when the problem sits BELOW the player; the anchor is their 80%-clear rating fitted over their WHOLE first-time history, so a player needs at least 20 rated attempts and a mixed record to enter; first-time attempts, one row per (user, problem), by 1-based position in the user's own first-time history

serve.gap_first25.note: mean rating gap over positions 1-25; mean of (the player's own anchor rating − the problem's shipped rating) in rating units, positive when the problem sits BELOW the player; the anchor is their 80%-clear rating fitted over their WHOLE first-time history, so a player needs at least 20 rated attempts and a mixed record to enter; first-time attempts, one row per (user, problem), by 1-based position in the user's own first-time history

serve.gapbin_clear_above2.note: clear rate where the player sits more than 2 rating units ABOVE the problem (gap >= 2); first-time clear rate in one bin of (player anchor rating − problem rating), bins half-open [lo, hi) in rating units; ± is the binomial standard error of that bin

serve.gapbin_clear_below2.note: clear rate where the player sits more than 2 rating units BELOW the problem (gap < -2); first-time clear rate in one bin of (player anchor rating − problem rating), bins half-open [lo, hi) in rating units; ± is the binomial standard error of that bin

serve.gapbin_clear_zero.note: clear rate within 0.1 of a rating unit of zero gap; in-sample, the player's anchor being fitted on these same attempts; first-time clear rate in one bin of (player anchor rating − problem rating), bins half-open [lo, hi) in rating units; ± is the binomial standard error of that bin

serve.gapbin_inversions.note: adjacent gap bins across the whole ladder whose clear rate FALLS as the gap rises; 0 is the monotone rise the response model implies

serve.gapbin_se_above2.note: ± on serve.gapbin_clear_above2; first-time clear rate in one bin of (player anchor rating − problem rating), bins half-open [lo, hi) in rating units; ± is the binomial standard error of that bin

serve.gapbin_se_below2.note: ± on serve.gapbin_clear_below2; first-time clear rate in one bin of (player anchor rating − problem rating), bins half-open [lo, hi) in rating units; ± is the binomial standard error of that bin

serve.gapbin_se_zero.note: ± on serve.gapbin_clear_zero; first-time clear rate in one bin of (player anchor rating − problem rating), bins half-open [lo, hi) in rating units; ± is the binomial standard error of that bin

serve.lapse_bound.note: largest global lapse the log admits: no attempt can clear more often than 1 − lapse, so the top gap bin's clear rate bounds it from above at 1 − that rate

serve.lapse_headroom.note: the log's lapse bound ÷ the shipped lapse — how far inside the bound the fitted value sits

serve.onboard_const_over3_pct.note: share served more than 3 ranks above true rank under a constant margin of 5 (simulated 20k, first 30 first-time attempts, 2000 seeded runs on the shipped 9×9 corpus)

serve.onboard_const_over5_pct.note: share served more than 5 ranks above true rank under a constant margin of 5 (simulated 20k, first 30 first-time attempts, 2000 seeded runs on the shipped 9×9 corpus)

serve.onboard_count_over3_pct.note: share served more than 3 ranks above true rank under a margin growing with the attempt count (simulated 20k, first 30 first-time attempts, 2000 seeded runs on the shipped 9×9 corpus)

serve.onboard_dan_attempts.note: first-time attempts before an unlimited-strength solver's SHOWN rank reaches 1 dan, under the shipped serve-gap cap

serve.onboard_dan_attempts_const.note: the same under a constant margin of 5

serve.onboard_dan_attempts_count.note: the same under a margin growing with the attempt count

serve.onboard_over3_pct.note: share served more than 3 ranks above true rank under the shipped serve-gap cap (simulated 20k, first 30 first-time attempts, 2000 seeded runs on the shipped 9×9 corpus)

serve.onboard_over5_pct.note: share served more than 5 ranks above true rank under the shipped serve-gap cap (simulated 20k, first 30 first-time attempts, 2000 seeded runs on the shipped 9×9 corpus)

slopescale.optimum_interior.note: 1 when no arm's sweep is lowest at an END of the swept grid, 0 when any is. READ THIS BEFORE QUOTING THE OTHERS: a minimum on a boundary means the grid did not contain the optimum, and every figure above is then a lower bound on the correction rather than a measurement of it. The fix is to widen the grid in pipeline/train_mirt.py and re-run the arms, never to quote the boundary point

slopescale.optimum_mult.note: the global slope multiplier at which the held-out score is lowest, averaged over 2 independent seeds of the shipped configuration. The multiplier pivots at the shipped rating, so the 80%-clear anchor is held and only the steepness moves; scored on HELD-ASIDE ROWS, not held-out users: the user is in the fit and their ability comes from their other attempts, which is the position the client is in when it predicts an attempt from a history — a different quantity from §1.10's stated one

slopescale.optimum_mult_min.note: the lowest per-seed optimum behind that average — the span the optimum itself moves over between fits differing only in the seed

slopescale.seed_spread_mnat.note: the spread between training seeds of the held-out score AT the shipped multiplier, in millinats — highest arm minus lowest. Defined the same way as the cost above, both being a peak-to-peak range of the same held-out score in the same units: that one ranges over two multipliers within one arm, this one over the arms at one multiplier. Each seed selects its own held-aside rows as well as its own initialization, which is what 'between two training seeds' means here

slopescale.seeds.note: independent training seeds of the SHIPPED configuration whose recorded slope-multiplier sweep backs every figure below. One seed counts once however many panels ran it, those runs being bitwise identical

slopescale.unity_cost_mnat.note: what the SHIPPED multiplier of 1 costs against each arm's own optimum, in millinats of held-out score, averaged over 2 independent seeds of the shipped configuration. Non-negative by construction, the shipped multiplier being one of the swept points; scored on HELD-ASIDE ROWS, not held-out users: the user is in the fit and their ability comes from their other attempts, which is the position the client is in when it predicts an attempt from a history — a different quantity from §1.10's stated one

slopescale.unity_inside_seed_spread.note: 1 when slopescale.unity_cost_mnat is strictly smaller than slopescale.seed_spread_mnat, 0 otherwise — §1.10's claim that the correction is smaller than the noise on the quantity it corrects, as a strict comparison of those two ledger values. An indicator for a `fig-guard: slopescale.unity_inside_seed_spread == 1`, never for a span

spread.halving_gain.note: whole minus halved spread, paired within each fit and averaged: what training on half a problem's attempts removes

spread.halving_gain_every_seed.note: 1 when that gain is positive in every fit. Backs a fig-guard

spread.info_loss_pct.note: Fisher information per attempt lost to the spread against every attempt sitting at its prediction, percent

spread.min_attempts.note: training rows a problem needs to be eligible for the holdout

spread.null_bias_sd.note: the estimator's mean on outcomes simulated with no departure, in units of its own spread; near zero when it is unbiased

spread.predicted_p05.note: 5th percentile of the model's predicted success on the whole set's rows, percent

spread.problems_halved.note: problems held out by half per fit, with at least one cross-user pair

spread.problems_whole.note: problems held out whole per fit, with at least one cross-user pair

spread.recoverable_pct.note: attempt-weighted share of a problem's departure variance that a shrunken per-problem estimate from the other attempts on it would recover, percent

spread.seeds.note: fits behind the spread figures, each with its own held-out draw

spread.tau_halved.note: the same spread on problems whose other half of attempts was trained on, mean over fits

spread.tau_halved_hi.note: highest per-fit 95% bootstrap upper bound, halved set

spread.tau_halved_lo.note: lowest per-fit 95% bootstrap lower bound, halved set

spread.tau_whole.note: spread of the problem's true logit about the fitted one, problems held out whole (features only), mean over fits

spread.tau_whole_hi.note: highest per-fit 95% bootstrap upper bound of that spread

spread.tau_whole_lo.note: lowest per-fit 95% bootstrap lower bound of that spread

spread.true_below60_pct.note: share of those rows whose implied true success is below 60%, percent

spread.true_p05.note: 5th percentile of the implied true success on those rows, percent

spread.true_p95.note: 95th percentile of the implied true success, percent

stopping.patience_advantage_best_mnat.note: the rule's BEST case over every seed and setting tried — the most it could claim under its own criterion

stopping.patience_advantage_mnat.note: millinats the selected epoch beats the FINAL epoch by on the held-aside rows, meaned over seeds and settings; SIGNED, so a negative value means the rule stops early and ships the worse fit. Flattering to the rule by construction: the selected epoch is a running minimum over the very rows the selection reads

stopping.patience_best_case_epoch.note: the epoch the rule stopped at in that best case. Read it beside the advantage: a rule can only match a budget it is competing with by declining to stop early, which is the budget's own answer arrived at expensively

stopping.patience_ever_beats_final.note: 1 if a patience rule beat the final epoch at any seed and any setting, 0 if it never did. An indicator for a fig-guard: 0 says the fixed budget is not merely lower-variance but better

stopping.patience_setting_over_seed_rati.note: the first spread over the second: how many times more the chosen epoch answers to the rule's own tuning than to the fit it is reading. Above one means the setting dominates

stopping.patience_spread_seeds.note: how far it moves when only the SEED changes, at a fixed setting, averaged over the settings — the same spread taken the other way round, over the same numbers

stopping.patience_spread_settings.note: how far the epoch a patience rule selects moves when only the PATIENCE SETTING changes, averaged over seeds — the rule's answer as a property of its own tuning

stopping.prob_tail_detrended_sd_mnat.note: and its detrended noise, on that unit

stopping.prob_tail_trend_mnat_per_500.note: the same slope on whole HELD-OUT PROBLEMS — the unit that can tell continued generalizing from continued fitting, and the criterion a budget belongs on. Flat here while the row split still descends is the ordinary shape of a budget that has arrived

stopping.seeds.note: seeds of the CONSTANT-RATE configuration whose recorded traces a patience rule is replayed on. They share one held-aside draw, so what separates two of them is the initialization alone

stopping.tail_detrended_sd_mnat.note: what is left of that window's spread once the slope is removed: the run-to-run noise, against which the raw spread overstates the noise by whatever the trend contributes

stopping.tail_trend_mnat_per_500.note: the SLOPE of the ROW-held-out score through the last third of the budget, millinats per 500 epochs, averaged over seeds. This is the trainer's convergence detector, whose rows share their users and problems with training — it keeps descending, which is why it is not what a budget is chosen on

swing.pass_only_baseline.note: published problems whose only resolved refutation is the pass, so excluding it would leave no ownership-swing measurement at all

swing.pass_outranks_stones_pct.note: share of the published problems where a resolved pass is the swing baseline over at least one resolved stone move

window.span_max_days.note: longest span in days of a FULL rank-estimator window — the 500 most recent first-time attempts — over the users who have that many; bounded from above by the length of the log

window.span_median_days.note: median span in days of a FULL rank-estimator window — the 500 most recent first-time attempts — over the users who have that many

window.span_over_90d.note: share of those users whose window spans more than 90 days; span in days of a FULL rank-estimator window — the 500 most recent first-time attempts — over the users who have that many

window.span_p75_days.note: upper-quartile span in days of a FULL rank-estimator window — the 500 most recent first-time attempts — over the users who have that many

_about: Measured figures the documents quote, one key per number. Written by `python -m ablations`; raw `value` + `fmt` are the record, `text` is derived. Never edit by hand — re-run the producer.
